he takes these herbs: seed of cress (ZÀ.AḪ.LI)
[keeps giving] it to him for seven days
he takes a bulb (gapanu) of garlic, a bulb of leek (GA.RAŠ)
he lets them in (to steep?), and [he sifts] them
[gives] it to him for seven days on an empty stomach(?)
he sews (it) into a leather cord (MATNU) (from an animal) which a leopard has killed
they take only the sinew of a ḫuitnaima- (wild animal?); he twists(?) (it) in, and he gets well
[The]n at night he entrusts it to the stars
he carries it into the house
Early in the morning, on an empty stomach(?), to drink
he sifts them, crushes (them), prepares (them) properly, and pours them into a leather tišni- (bag?)
from the fish he removes the inner parts
